criterion: Recovery is possible and the error names it
description: After `client revoke --kind agent`, `agent-grant` for that harness says 'Harness is not enrolled on this device; join an Agent invitation first'. Doing exactly that (new Agent invitation, `client join --harness openai-codex`) succeeds and uses up the invitation, but the grant is still refused, because the harness maps to the same deterministic Actor ID that stays in revokedActors. There is no way back for that harness in the project, and the error sends the person in a loop.
expected: Either a supported un-revoke/re-enrol path, or an explicit 'This agent was revoked for this project; it cannot be re-enrolled' error (and the join refuses instead of consuming the invitation).
actual: Join succeeds silently; grant keeps returning the same misleading advice.
suggested_fix: Return a REVOKED-specific error from agent-grant and from join for a revoked Actor; decide and document whether re-enrolment issues a new Actor.

description: A revoked agent looks identical to an active offline agent on the board: same avatar, 'Offline' profile, Devices list, and no revocation entry in Activity.
expected: Profile and avatar show 'Revoked' (or the agent leaves the active stack) and Activity records who revoked it and when.
suggested_fix: Expose revocation state in the project actor list and add an Activity event.

description: The revoked agent's credential on the hub returns `AUTH_REQUIRED: Open Pardner through client open to authenticate`; the same revocation on the replica returns `REVOKED: Project access revoked; local data remains saved`.
expected: Both return REVOKED with agent-appropriate wording.
suggested_fix: Map revoked agent sessions to a REVOKED error in client-auth.

description: `client revoke --kind agent --id actor-nope` (an ID that does not exist) returns `FORBIDDEN: Agent belongs to another human`.
expected: `NOT_FOUND: No agent actor-nope in this project`.
actual: Permission error for a missing Actor.
